dataBundleRecords.label: Drainage network of the catchment (drainage_network 1.0.0)
dataBundleRecords.license: Licence for Copernicus DEM instance COP-DEM-GLO-30-F Global 30m Full, Free & Open
dataBundleRecords.attribution: Catchment derived by Siterra from Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (2021 release); Produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-30 © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved; The organisations in charge of the Copernicus programme by law or by delegation do not incur any liability for any use of the Copernicus WorldDEM-30; Flow direction and depression fill depth conditioned by a private step that uses pysheds 0.5 (Bartos 2020, GPL-3.0, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3822494); the software is not part of this bundle

limitations: The network is drawn from a 30 m surface model, not mapped on the ground: trees, buildings, steep walls and radar artefacts distort the surface, and the D8 path can leave the real channel. No stream was checked in the field.

A segment is drawn wherever 1.0 km2 or more drains to a cell. The network's extent and length follow that threshold; it is not a measured channel head, and it does not separate streams that run all year from streams that run only after rain or snowmelt.

Depression filling and flat resolution route flow across closed hollows and the lower gorge, so some segments run where the 30 m surface rises along the line. Those segments are flagged, their heights are stored unchanged, and the line says nothing about how water moves there.

Upstream area counts the cells that drain to a point along D8 paths on the filled surface. It is not the share of rain that reaches the point, and it ignores irrigation canals, withdrawals and groundwater.
Strahler order counts how channels join. It says nothing about channel size, discharge or whether water is present.

Heights are metres above the EGM2008 geoid from the Copernicus DEM GLO-30 surface model, whose stated absolute vertical accuracy is under 4 m (90% linear error) and relative vertical accuracy under 2 m on slopes up to 20% and under 4 m above, as arithmetic means with local deviations possible (Copernicus DEM Product Handbook 5.0).
The catchment is a hydrological analysis extent, not a pasture, agdal or management boundary.

(2022), https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7254221, CC BY 4.0

limitations: One pixel is an illustration, not a sample: it was chosen by judgment among the candidates of a rule (the selection record gives their number and its rank), and it says nothing about other pixels.

The class spectra come from one clear day, the cells of each class inside this pixel, and one 2021 land cover map. They are not typical spectra of the classes, and a 10 m cell at the edge of a class mixes surfaces.

The mix model assumes the pixel's reflectance is the share-weighted sum of its class medians. It ignores shadow, slope and variation inside a class, so its NDVI is modelled, not measured, and it differs from the measured pixel NDVI by the amount stored.

NDVI measures how green the ground looks from above, not forage, palatability or species: in Ait Bouguemez and the Central High Atlas, upper rangelands are dominated by spiny xerophytic vegetation over reduced short grasslands (SCI-19, p. 2), and on the valley floor tree cover may include orchards (SCI-03, pp. 5, 9 to 10).

The 26-season series is the pixel's own March to June greenness, not adjusted for rainfall. Its trend is a descriptive Theil-Sen slope with Sen's 95% interval, and no p-value or false discovery rate class is stored for one pixel (SCI-52).

Terra's overpass has drifted earlier since 2020, from 10:30 to about 9:06 mean local time by December 2025 (NASA), so later seasons are seen with a lower sun and longer shadows in mountain terrain, which may shift NDVI without any change on the ground.
The catchment is a hydrological analysis extent, not a pasture, agdal or management boundary.

(2022), https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7254221, CC BY 4.0

limitations: Each pixel's interval is one of thousands. With no change anywhere, about 2.5% of pixels would still show an upward and 2.5% a downward interval at the 95% level, so the shares are shown beside a false discovery rate check (Benjamini and Hochberg 1995, q = 0.05), the control Wilks (2016) recommends when many locations are tested at once, and the map shows the slope only, not which pixels pass.

Neighbouring pixels are not independent: they share weather, snow and sensor effects. A connected area of pixels can arise from one shared cause, and the false discovery rate procedure was proved for independent tests.
Each 250 m MODIS pixel mixes surfaces. Land cover shares use ESA WorldCover 2021, a single 2021 map, applied to every season.

NDVI measures how green the ground looks from above, not forage, palatability or species: in Ait Bouguemez and the Central High Atlas, upper rangelands are dominated by spiny xerophytic vegetation over reduced short grasslands (SCI-19, p. 2), herders report the loss of palatable species (Astragalus armatus, Thymus satureioides) and the spread of unpalatable plants (Thymelaea virgata, Euphorbia nicaeensis) (SCI-03, pp. 7 to 8), and valley-floor apple orchards and irrigated fodder have expanded (SCI-03, pp. 5, 9 to 10; SCI-19, p. 9; SCI-105).

The June to September window spans the transition from late-spring pastoral agdal closure into open summer high-pasture grazing before transhumant flocks leave the valley in September and October (SCI-03, pp. 5 to 6, 12; SCI-19, pp. 2 to 5, Table 1; SCI-96); exact opening dates vary by village assembly and year.
These trends are not adjusted for rainfall; restrend_long_record states how closely the place's greenness follows antecedent rain.

Trend methods can miss real change: in simulations for southern Africa, 30 to 40% degradation was needed before a trend showed under a rainfall-driven increase (Wessels et al. 2012). An interval that includes zero is not evidence of no change.

In the spring windows, upper slopes are snow-covered for part of the window. Composites keep only pixels flagged good or marginal, but earlier or later snowmelt can change spring greenness with no change in the plants.

Terra's overpass has drifted earlier since 2020, from 10:30 to about 9:06 mean local time by December 2025 (NASA): later seasons are seen with a lower sun and longer shadows in mountain terrain, which may shift NDVI without any change on the ground.

limitations: Each stratum and window pair has its own interval. With many shown together, some intervals will exclude zero by chance alone, so the false discovery rate check (Benjamini and Hochberg 1995, q = 0.05) is stated beside every pair, and every pair is shown.

Each 250 m MODIS pixel mixes surfaces; stratum values weight pixels by how much of the stratum falls inside them, so a mixed pixel counts toward more than one stratum. Land cover groups use ESA WorldCover 2021, a single 2021 map, applied to every season.

NDVI measures how green the ground looks from above, not forage, palatability or species: in Ait Bouguemez and the Central High Atlas, upper rangelands are dominated by spiny xerophytic vegetation over reduced short grasslands (SCI-19, p. 2), herders report the loss of palatable species (Astragalus armatus, Thymus satureioides) and the spread of unpalatable plants (Thymelaea virgata, Euphorbia nicaeensis) (SCI-03, pp. 7 to 8), and valley-floor apple orchards and irrigated fodder have expanded (SCI-03, pp. 5, 9 to 10; SCI-19, p. 9; SCI-105).

The June to September window spans the transition from late-spring pastoral agdal closure into open summer high-pasture grazing before transhumant flocks leave the valley in September and October (SCI-03, pp. 5 to 6, 12; SCI-19, pp. 2 to 5, Table 1; SCI-96); exact opening dates vary by village assembly and year.
These trends are not adjusted for rainfall; restrend_long_record states how closely the place's greenness follows antecedent rain.

Trend methods can miss real change: in simulations for southern Africa, 30 to 40% degradation was needed before a trend showed under a rainfall-driven increase (Wessels et al. 2012). An interval that includes zero is not evidence of no change.

In the spring windows, upper slopes are snow-covered for part of the window. Composites keep only pixels flagged good or marginal, but earlier or later snowmelt can change spring greenness with no change in the plants.

Terra's overpass has drifted earlier since 2020, from 10:30 to about 9:06 mean local time by December 2025 (NASA): later seasons are seen with a lower sun and longer shadows in mountain terrain, which may shift NDVI without any change on the ground.

Against 448 Sentinel-2 scenes of the Atlas, Terra MODIS snow cover (version 6) was underestimated by 6.13% on average with the global NDSI threshold of 0.4 and overestimated by 0.34% with the Atlas threshold of 0.2 (Bousbaa et al. 2024). Both thresholds are shown.

Against five Atlas stations, MOD10A1 (version 5) agreed with snow observations 89% of the time (2000 to 2013, other Atlas catchments; Marchane et al. 2015). There is no station comparison for this valley.
Each 500 m pixel is called snow-covered or not as a whole; patchy snow, thin snow and snow on shaded slopes can be missed.
Snow cover is not snow depth or water: it says nothing about how much water the snow holds.

Terra's overpass has drifted earlier since 2020, from 10:30 to about 9:06 mean local time by December 2025 (NASA), so later years are seen with a lower sun and longer shadows, which may change snow detection on steep slopes.

limitations: A profile is read from a 30 m surface model: trees, buildings, steep walls and radar artefacts distort it, and narrow gorges such as the lower gorge near the outlet are not resolved. Heights are metres above the EGM2008 geoid with the DEM's stated vertical accuracy (Copernicus DEM Product Handbook 5.0).
Samples are 30 m apart, so a band crossing or a land cover boundary is placed to within about 15 m, and a feature narrower than 30 m can fall between samples.
Land cover is ESA WorldCover 2021 at 10 m, a single 2021 map applied to the line: tree cover on the valley floor may include orchards, and no class is a pasture, agdal or management unit.
An elevation band is a stratum that organises sampling, cut from the elevation distribution of the catchment; it is not a vegetation type, a grazing zone or a management boundary.
The valley floor segment follows the published elevation range of the valley floor (1800 to 2200 m, SCI-19); it is not a measured flat bottom.

The valley axis is the longest flow path of a D8 network, which follows the main river, not the centre line of the valley; its profile inherits the limits of the drainage network, including places where the surface rises along the line.
The catchment is a hydrological analysis extent, not a pasture, agdal or management boundary.

measurementRecords.aggregation: Total length of the drawn drainage segments (headline.length_km_total).

limitations: The network is drawn from a 30 m surface model, not mapped on the ground: trees, buildings, steep walls and radar artefacts distort the surface, and the D8 path can leave the real channel. No stream was checked in the field.

A segment is drawn wherever 1.0 km2 or more drains to a cell. The network's extent and length follow that threshold; it is not a measured channel head, and it does not separate streams that run all year from streams that run only after rain or snowmelt.

Depression filling and flat resolution route flow across closed hollows and the lower gorge, so some segments run where the 30 m surface rises along the line. Those segments are flagged, their heights are stored unchanged, and the line says nothing about how water moves there.

Upstream area counts the cells that drain to a point along D8 paths on the filled surface. It is not the share of rain that reaches the point, and it ignores irrigation canals, withdrawals and groundwater.
Strahler order counts how channels join. It says nothing about channel size, discharge or whether water is present.

Heights are metres above the EGM2008 geoid from the Copernicus DEM GLO-30 surface model, whose stated absolute vertical accuracy is under 4 m (90% linear error) and relative vertical accuracy under 2 m on slopes up to 20% and under 4 m above, as arithmetic means with local deviations possible (Copernicus DEM Product Handbook 5.0).
The catchment is a hydrological analysis extent, not a pasture, agdal or management boundary.

measurementRecords.aggregation: Number of MODIS 250 m pixels the catchment touches (modis_pixels_touched).

limitations: Each pixel's interval is one of thousands. With no change anywhere, about 2.5% of pixels would still show an upward and 2.5% a downward interval at the 95% level, so the shares are shown beside a false discovery rate check (Benjamini and Hochberg 1995, q = 0.05), the control Wilks (2016) recommends when many locations are tested at once, and the map shows the slope only, not which pixels pass.

Neighbouring pixels are not independent: they share weather, snow and sensor effects. A connected area of pixels can arise from one shared cause, and the false discovery rate procedure was proved for independent tests.
Each 250 m MODIS pixel mixes surfaces. Land cover shares use ESA WorldCover 2021, a single 2021 map, applied to every season.

NDVI measures how green the ground looks from above, not forage, palatability or species: in Ait Bouguemez and the Central High Atlas, upper rangelands are dominated by spiny xerophytic vegetation over reduced short grasslands (SCI-19, p. 2), herders report the loss of palatable species (Astragalus armatus, Thymus satureioides) and the spread of unpalatable plants (Thymelaea virgata, Euphorbia nicaeensis) (SCI-03, pp. 7 to 8), and valley-floor apple orchards and irrigated fodder have expanded (SCI-03, pp. 5, 9 to 10; SCI-19, p. 9; SCI-105).

The June to September window spans the transition from late-spring pastoral agdal closure into open summer high-pasture grazing before transhumant flocks leave the valley in September and October (SCI-03, pp. 5 to 6, 12; SCI-19, pp. 2 to 5, Table 1; SCI-96); exact opening dates vary by village assembly and year.
These trends are not adjusted for rainfall; restrend_long_record states how closely the place's greenness follows antecedent rain.

Trend methods can miss real change: in simulations for southern Africa, 30 to 40% degradation was needed before a trend showed under a rainfall-driven increase (Wessels et al. 2012). An interval that includes zero is not evidence of no change.

In the spring windows, upper slopes are snow-covered for part of the window. Composites keep only pixels flagged good or marginal, but earlier or later snowmelt can change spring greenness with no change in the plants.

Terra's overpass has drifted earlier since 2020, from 10:30 to about 9:06 mean local time by December 2025 (NASA): later seasons are seen with a lower sun and longer shadows in mountain terrain, which may shift NDVI without any change on the ground.

measurementRecords.unit: fraction of the band's 10 m cells, 0 to 1
measurementRecords.aggregation: Highest of the monthly clear shares of the upper elevation band (2815.2 m and above), December to March 2019 to 2025, a month counted when at least one clear Sentinel-2 date exists (any_date validity) (bands.3.winter.any_date.highest).

limitations: A clear share counts cells that have at least one (or three) Sentinel-2 dates not classed as cloud, cloud shadow, snow or water in the month; it says how often the band was seen, not how much of it was covered by snow or cloud, and the files do not say which of the two hid a cell.
The shares depend on the Sentinel-2 scene classification of each date, which makes errors on thin cloud, snow edges and shadow; they are observations of the classification, not of the ground.
Bands are elevation terciles that organise sampling; they are not vegetation types, grazing zones or management boundaries.
Only the months of 2019 to 2025 that the Sentinel-2 monthly series holds are covered, 28 winter months.

measurementRecords.aggregation: Number of the pixel's 10 m analysis cells of WorldCover 2021 class bare or sparse vegetation that were kept for the 11 June 2025 spectra (scene classification 4 or 5 and every band above zero); every footprint cell was kept (spectra.classes[].cells_kept).

limitations: One pixel is an illustration, not a sample: it was chosen by judgment among the candidates of a rule (the selection record gives their number and its rank), and it says nothing about other pixels.

The class spectra come from one clear day, the cells of each class inside this pixel, and one 2021 land cover map. They are not typical spectra of the classes, and a 10 m cell at the edge of a class mixes surfaces.

The mix model assumes the pixel's reflectance is the share-weighted sum of its class medians. It ignores shadow, slope and variation inside a class, so its NDVI is modelled, not measured, and it differs from the measured pixel NDVI by the amount stored.

NDVI measures how green the ground looks from above, not forage, palatability or species: in Ait Bouguemez and the Central High Atlas, upper rangelands are dominated by spiny xerophytic vegetation over reduced short grasslands (SCI-19, p. 2), and on the valley floor tree cover may include orchards (SCI-03, pp. 5, 9 to 10).

The 26-season series is the pixel's own March to June greenness, not adjusted for rainfall. Its trend is a descriptive Theil-Sen slope with Sen's 95% interval, and no p-value or false discovery rate class is stored for one pixel (SCI-52).

Terra's overpass has drifted earlier since 2020, from 10:30 to about 9:06 mean local time by December 2025 (NASA), so later seasons are seen with a lower sun and longer shadows in mountain terrain, which may shift NDVI without any change on the ground.
The catchment is a hydrological analysis extent, not a pasture, agdal or management boundary.

limitations: Each pixel's interval is one of thousands. With no change anywhere, about 2.5% of pixels would still show an upward and 2.5% a downward interval at the 95% level, so the shares are shown beside a false discovery rate check (Benjamini and Hochberg 1995, q = 0.05), the control Wilks (2016) recommends when many locations are tested at once, and the map shows the slope only, not which pixels pass.

Neighbouring pixels are not independent: they share weather, snow and sensor effects. A connected area of pixels can arise from one shared cause, and the false discovery rate procedure was proved for independent tests.
Each 250 m MODIS pixel mixes surfaces. Land cover shares use ESA WorldCover 2021, a single 2021 map, applied to every season.

NDVI measures how green the ground looks from above, not forage, palatability or species: in Ait Bouguemez and the Central High Atlas, upper rangelands are dominated by spiny xerophytic vegetation over reduced short grasslands (SCI-19, p. 2), herders report the loss of palatable species (Astragalus armatus, Thymus satureioides) and the spread of unpalatable plants (Thymelaea virgata, Euphorbia nicaeensis) (SCI-03, pp. 7 to 8), and valley-floor apple orchards and irrigated fodder have expanded (SCI-03, pp. 5, 9 to 10; SCI-19, p. 9; SCI-105).

The June to September window spans the transition from late-spring pastoral agdal closure into open summer high-pasture grazing before transhumant flocks leave the valley in September and October (SCI-03, pp. 5 to 6, 12; SCI-19, pp. 2 to 5, Table 1; SCI-96); exact opening dates vary by village assembly and year.
These trends are not adjusted for rainfall; restrend_long_record states how closely the place's greenness follows antecedent rain.

Trend methods can miss real change: in simulations for southern Africa, 30 to 40% degradation was needed before a trend showed under a rainfall-driven increase (Wessels et al. 2012). An interval that includes zero is not evidence of no change.

limitations: The rainfall-adjusted residual still holds everything else that changes greenness: temperature, snow, irrigation, orchards and fields, grazing, fire, and sensor or orbit changes. It is not a measure of grazing impact or of degradation.

An interval that includes zero is not evidence of no change.
Each 250 m MODIS pixel mixes surfaces; stratum values weight pixels by how much of the stratum falls inside them, so a mixed pixel counts toward more than one stratum.

In winter months the accepted pixels favour the valley floor and south-facing slopes, because snow and shade remove the others; the area value then describes those pixels, not the whole catchment.
The spatial IQR is variability across pixels, not a confidence interval.
No cropland or irrigation mask is applied in this version: valley-floor fields and orchards are inside the summary.
Processing baselines differ across the record (mostly 05.00 for 2019 to 2021, 04.00 for 2022, 05.09 to 05.11 later); same-acquisition comparisons differ by about 0.002 to 0.003 reflectance.
Seven years is a short record; nothing here is a trend or a degradation finding.
Cloud and snow shares are counted per tile observation; the 29SQR and 29RQQ overlap counts twice.

Revision 13 (2026-10-27). Among duplicates of a tile and date, an item with no clear pixels over the catchment is now skipped when a twin has some. That clause was added to the duplicate rule after data was first read; the rule fixed before any data was read kept the newest processing baseline only. Revision 12, the first committed, has no version field; it documented the clause but kept the newest item, so it kept an item with 0 clear pixels over the catchment on seven tile-dates: 29RQQ 2019-04-17 (twin had 285 clear pixels), 2019-06-21 (702,669), 2020-11-12 (84), 2021-06-07 (8), 2021-11-19 (8), 2021-12-22 (8), and 29SQR 2020-10-23 (16). In five cases the twin is an older baseline (02.14, 03.00, 03.01), so its clear pixels come from an older scene classification. This revision recomputes 2019-04, 2019-06, 2020-10, 2020-11, 2021-06, 2021-11 and 2021-12 and everything derived from them; no NDVI or departure area median moved at four decimals.

limitations: Reduced QA (scene classification only): snow, snow edges and terrain shadow can survive the mask.
In winter months the accepted pixels favour the valley floor and south-facing slopes, because snow and shade remove the others; the area value then describes those pixels, not the whole catchment.
The spatial IQR is variability across pixels, not a confidence interval.
No cropland or irrigation mask is applied in this version: valley-floor fields and orchards are inside the summary.
Processing baselines differ across the record (mostly 05.00 for 2019 to 2021, 04.00 for 2022, 05.09 to 05.11 later); same-acquisition comparisons differ by about 0.002 to 0.003 reflectance.
Seven years is a short record; nothing here is a trend or a degradation finding.

measurementRecords.aggregation: The lower elevation band limit that the meridian crosses (tabant_meridian.band_crossings[0].boundary_m), the equal-area tercile limit of the terrain strata.

limitations: A profile is read from a 30 m surface model: trees, buildings, steep walls and radar artefacts distort it, and narrow gorges such as the lower gorge near the outlet are not resolved. Heights are metres above the EGM2008 geoid with the DEM's stated vertical accuracy (Copernicus DEM Product Handbook 5.0).
Samples are 30 m apart, so a band crossing or a land cover boundary is placed to within about 15 m, and a feature narrower than 30 m can fall between samples.
Land cover is ESA WorldCover 2021 at 10 m, a single 2021 map applied to the line: tree cover on the valley floor may include orchards, and no class is a pasture, agdal or management unit.
An elevation band is a stratum that organises sampling, cut from the elevation distribution of the catchment; it is not a vegetation type, a grazing zone or a management boundary.
The valley floor segment follows the published elevation range of the valley floor (1800 to 2200 m, SCI-19); it is not a measured flat bottom.

The valley axis is the longest flow path of a D8 network, which follows the main river, not the centre line of the valley; its profile inherits the limits of the drainage network, including places where the surface rises along the line.
The catchment is a hydrological analysis extent, not a pasture, agdal or management boundary.

uncertainty.method: 95% interval (level 0.95) of the ordinary least squares slope of growing-season NDVI on season year (ols block).

limitations: Each stratum and window pair has its own interval. With many shown together, some intervals will exclude zero by chance alone, so the false discovery rate check (Benjamini and Hochberg 1995, q = 0.05) is stated beside every pair, and every pair is shown.

Each 250 m MODIS pixel mixes surfaces; stratum values weight pixels by how much of the stratum falls inside them, so a mixed pixel counts toward more than one stratum. Land cover groups use ESA WorldCover 2021, a single 2021 map, applied to every season.

NDVI measures how green the ground looks from above, not forage, palatability or species: in Ait Bouguemez and the Central High Atlas, upper rangelands are dominated by spiny xerophytic vegetation over reduced short grasslands (SCI-19, p. 2), herders report the loss of palatable species (Astragalus armatus, Thymus satureioides) and the spread of unpalatable plants (Thymelaea virgata, Euphorbia nicaeensis) (SCI-03, pp. 7 to 8), and valley-floor apple orchards and irrigated fodder have expanded (SCI-03, pp. 5, 9 to 10; SCI-19, p. 9; SCI-105).

The June to September window spans the transition from late-spring pastoral agdal closure into open summer high-pasture grazing before transhumant flocks leave the valley in September and October (SCI-03, pp. 5 to 6, 12; SCI-19, pp. 2 to 5, Table 1; SCI-96); exact opening dates vary by village assembly and year.
These trends are not adjusted for rainfall; restrend_long_record states how closely the place's greenness follows antecedent rain.

Trend methods can miss real change: in simulations for southern Africa, 30 to 40% degradation was needed before a trend showed under a rainfall-driven increase (Wessels et al. 2012). An interval that includes zero is not evidence of no change.

In the spring windows, upper slopes are snow-covered for part of the window. Composites keep only pixels flagged good or marginal, but earlier or later snowmelt can change spring greenness with no change in the plants.

Terra's overpass has drifted earlier since 2020, from 10:30 to about 9:06 mean local time by December 2025 (NASA): later seasons are seen with a lower sun and longer shadows in mountain terrain, which may shift NDVI without any change on the ground.

No rain gauge in or near the valley was compared with these values.
CHIRPS v3.0 fills missing satellite data with ERA5 and adjusts stations for gauge undercatch, so it is overall wetter than v2.0; never splice v2 and v3.
The 1991 to 2020 mean is a reference for departures, not a drought index; no SPI or percent of normal is computed.
Snowfall and snowmelt timing are not represented by a monthly precipitation total.

temporalObservationRecords.seasonDefinition: Calendar month 2019-01 (UTC, start inclusive, end exclusive)

limitations: The reference is a short period (2019 to 2025), not a climate normal.
A departure describes how this month differs from other years here; it does not say why.
The spatial IQR is variability across pixels, not a confidence interval.
In winter months the accepted pixels favour the valley floor and south-facing slopes, because snow and shade remove the others; the area value then describes those pixels, not the whole catchment.

Revision 13 (2026-10-27). Among duplicates of a tile and date, an item with no clear pixels over the catchment is now skipped when a twin has some. That clause was added to the duplicate rule after data was first read; the rule fixed before any data was read kept the newest processing baseline only. Revision 12, the first committed, has no version field; it documented the clause but kept the newest item, so it kept an item with 0 clear pixels over the catchment on seven tile-dates: 29RQQ 2019-04-17 (twin had 285 clear pixels), 2019-06-21 (702,669), 2020-11-12 (84), 2021-06-07 (8), 2021-11-19 (8), 2021-12-22 (8), and 29SQR 2020-10-23 (16). In five cases the twin is an older baseline (02.14, 03.00, 03.01), so its clear pixels come from an older scene classification. This revision recomputes 2019-04, 2019-06, 2020-10, 2020-11, 2021-06, 2021-11 and 2021-12 and everything derived from them; no NDVI or departure area median moved at four decimals.

Revision 14 (2026-10-27). The leave-one-year-out measurements of 2019-03 and 2020-03, which revision 13 excluded without saying why, now carry a missing_reason (Siterra STAC extension 1.1.0): pixels with a value that year and a reference from at least 4 other years cover too little of the catchment, below the 70% coverage policy. No value, status or count changed. Only this bundle is revised; the aligned bundle's link to it is re-pinned, and its results are unchanged.

Revision 15 (2026-10-28). Each period whose leave-one-year-out departure is available (56 of 84) gains a display raster for the map, asset overview: that period's per-pixel leave-one-year-out departure, averaged into 30 m Web Mercator cells (about 25.5 m on the ground here) and painted on the fixed scale -0.10 to +0.10 with the light-theme NDVI departure ramp, lossless WebP. It is for display only; every number shown comes from the measurements. 2019-03 and 2020-03, whose leave-one-year-out value is excluded, and the periods without a departure have no display raster. The Collection also lists the mapped cropland and buildings (ESA WorldCover 2021 classes 40 and 50) of the terrain strata bundle as polygons, for the map's hatch; no value is masked by them. No value, status or count changed. Only this bundle is revised; the aligned bundle's link to it is re-pinned, and its results are unchanged.

In winter months the accepted pixels favour the valley floor and south-facing slopes, because snow and shade remove the others; the area value then describes those pixels, not the whole catchment.
The spatial IQR is variability across pixels, not a confidence interval.
No cropland or irrigation mask is applied in this version: valley-floor fields and orchards are inside the summary.
Processing baselines differ across the record (mostly 05.00 for 2019 to 2021, 04.00 for 2022, 05.09 to 05.11 later); same-acquisition comparisons differ by about 0.002 to 0.003 reflectance.
Seven years is a short record; nothing here is a trend or a degradation finding.
Cloud and snow shares are counted per tile observation; the 29SQR and 29RQQ overlap counts twice.

Revision 13 (2026-10-27). Among duplicates of a tile and date, an item with no clear pixels over the catchment is now skipped when a twin has some. That clause was added to the duplicate rule after data was first read; the rule fixed before any data was read kept the newest processing baseline only. Revision 12, the first committed, has no version field; it documented the clause but kept the newest item, so it kept an item with 0 clear pixels over the catchment on seven tile-dates: 29RQQ 2019-04-17 (twin had 285 clear pixels), 2019-06-21 (702,669), 2020-11-12 (84), 2021-06-07 (8), 2021-11-19 (8), 2021-12-22 (8), and 29SQR 2020-10-23 (16). In five cases the twin is an older baseline (02.14, 03.00, 03.01), so its clear pixels come from an older scene classification. This revision recomputes 2019-04, 2019-06, 2020-10, 2020-11, 2021-06, 2021-11 and 2021-12 and everything derived from them; no NDVI or departure area median moved at four decimals.

contextFeatureRecords.name: Drainage lines, Strahler order 1
contextFeatureRecords.method: The 117 segments of Strahler order 1 in the asset drainage_lines of bundle_drainage_network_ait_bouguemez, copied as the bundle lists them. A D8 path on a 30 m surface, a model estimate; segment attributes stay in the asset.
contextFeatureRecords.attribution: Catchment derived by Siterra from Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (2021 release); Produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-30 © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved; The organisations in charge of the Copernicus programme by law or by delegation do not incur any liability for any use of the Copernicus WorldDEM-30; Flow direction and depression fill depth conditioned by a private step that uses pysheds 0.5 (Bartos 2020, GPL-3.0, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3822494); the software is not part of this bundle
contextFeatureRecords.license: Licence for Copernicus DEM instance COP-DEM-GLO-30-F Global 30m Full, Free & Open
limitations: The network is drawn from a 30 m surface model, not mapped on the ground: trees, buildings, steep walls and radar artefacts distort the surface, and the D8 path can leave the real channel. No stream was checked in the field.

A segment is drawn wherever 1.0 km2 or more drains to a cell. The network's extent and length follow that threshold; it is not a measured channel head, and it does not separate streams that run all year from streams that run only after rain or snowmelt.

Depression filling and flat resolution route flow across closed hollows and the lower gorge, so some segments run where the 30 m surface rises along the line. Those segments are flagged, their heights are stored unchanged, and the line says nothing about how water moves there.

Upstream area counts the cells that drain to a point along D8 paths on the filled surface. It is not the share of rain that reaches the point, and it ignores irrigation canals, withdrawals and groundwater.
Strahler order counts how channels join. It says nothing about channel size, discharge or whether water is present.

Heights are metres above the EGM2008 geoid from the Copernicus DEM GLO-30 surface model, whose stated absolute vertical accuracy is under 4 m (90% linear error) and relative vertical accuracy under 2 m on slopes up to 20% and under 4 m above, as arithmetic means with local deviations possible (Copernicus DEM Product Handbook 5.0).
The catchment is a hydrological analysis extent, not a pasture, agdal or management boundary.

limitations: A profile is read from a 30 m surface model: trees, buildings, steep walls and radar artefacts distort it, and narrow gorges such as the lower gorge near the outlet are not resolved. Heights are metres above the EGM2008 geoid with the DEM's stated vertical accuracy (Copernicus DEM Product Handbook 5.0).
Samples are 30 m apart, so a band crossing or a land cover boundary is placed to within about 15 m, and a feature narrower than 30 m can fall between samples.
Land cover is ESA WorldCover 2021 at 10 m, a single 2021 map applied to the line: tree cover on the valley floor may include orchards, and no class is a pasture, agdal or management unit.
An elevation band is a stratum that organises sampling, cut from the elevation distribution of the catchment; it is not a vegetation type, a grazing zone or a management boundary.
The valley floor segment follows the published elevation range of the valley floor (1800 to 2200 m, SCI-19); it is not a measured flat bottom.

The valley axis is the longest flow path of a D8 network, which follows the main river, not the centre line of the valley; its profile inherits the limits of the drainage network, including places where the surface rises along the line.
The catchment is a hydrological analysis extent, not a pasture, agdal or management boundary.

limitations: A profile is read from a 30 m surface model: trees, buildings, steep walls and radar artefacts distort it, and narrow gorges such as the lower gorge near the outlet are not resolved. Heights are metres above the EGM2008 geoid with the DEM's stated vertical accuracy (Copernicus DEM Product Handbook 5.0).
Samples are 30 m apart, so a band crossing or a land cover boundary is placed to within about 15 m, and a feature narrower than 30 m can fall between samples.
Land cover is ESA WorldCover 2021 at 10 m, a single 2021 map applied to the line: tree cover on the valley floor may include orchards, and no class is a pasture, agdal or management unit.
An elevation band is a stratum that organises sampling, cut from the elevation distribution of the catchment; it is not a vegetation type, a grazing zone or a management boundary.
The valley floor segment follows the published elevation range of the valley floor (1800 to 2200 m, SCI-19); it is not a measured flat bottom.

The valley axis is the longest flow path of a D8 network, which follows the main river, not the centre line of the valley; its profile inherits the limits of the drainage network, including places where the surface rises along the line.
The catchment is a hydrological analysis extent, not a pasture, agdal or management boundary.
